title_en: A New Playbook for University Endowments 11/2/26
title_zh: 大学捐赠基金的新打法：对话 State Street 的 Anna Paglia 与 CapTrust 的 Mike Vogelzang
subtitle_zh: 从 UCBG 到私募信贷 ETF，看 ETF 如何融合公私市场、把捐赠基金策略普惠给普通投资者。
summary_zh: 本期 ETF Edge 由 Dominic Chu 主持，对话 State Street Investment Management 首席业务官 Anna Paglia 与 CapTrust 首席投资官 Mike Vogelzang，核心议题是公开市场与私募投资的融合，以及 ETF 如何把大学捐赠基金（endowment）策略普惠给普通投资者。节目的抓手是九月上市的 UCBG（UC Blue and Gold）捐赠基金 ETF：它源自 State Street 与 University of California Investments 长期共管的策略，凭借来自 UC 捐赠基金体系高达二十五亿美元的锚定投资（anchor investment），成为美国上市 ETF 史上规模最大的一次发行。Paglia 强调这不是重新发明，而是联合 S&P 等指数伙伴，把原本主动的策略装进可预测、可复制、可规模化的指数外壳，用不同法律载体打通渠道。Vogelzang 则提醒捐赠基金并非千篇一律，除 Ford Foundation、常春藤等巨头外，还有大量规模在两千万至两亿五千万美元之间的小型捐赠基金同样需要打理；UCBG 用九成 S&P 500 加一成投资级债券的简单敞口，像一个一键搞定的轻松按钮，但对 Mag 7 主导、偏成长的指数存在集中度隐忧。两人还谈到 ETF 通过每日价格披露与申购赎回机制，为私募信贷等缺乏价格发现（price discovery）的资产创造流动性与透明度，以及 State Street 借单一伞形份额类别化解碎片化成本、让 DC 计划也能触及 ETF 创新。是一集关于捐赠基金策略普惠化的方法论深谈。

turns.en: So I just want to follow up there, because the interesting points are there with regard to just the track record, the training aspect and whether people want to get in and out of this particular fund. And yes, we do see more mature funds get it. I think my focus and my question to you is, if we have these types of products, Mike,
turns.zh: 我想就这一点接着追问，因为有意思的点就在于业绩记录、这方面的历练，以及人们是否愿意进出这只特定的基金。是的，我们确实看到更成熟的基金会做到这点。我想我的重点、我要问你的问题是，Mike，如果我们有这类产品，

turns.zh: 它们是交易所交易的，是用来模仿流动性策略的——短期债券以及像 S&P 500 那种流动性好的股票——而且我们能以更低成本做到。这是一回事。那么你是否感觉到，在你的客户群、在你服务的那些围绕捐赠基金和基金会的客户当中，有更多的倾斜？

turns.en: Do you feel as though they're tilting a little bit more towards liquid type exchange traded products, or are they still kind of moving towards hedge fund private equity, private credit, and other real estate type investments as kind of more around their portfolios than say the liquid stuff? Yeah, that's an exact...
turns.zh: 你是否觉得他们正更多地倾向于流动性类型的交易所交易产品，还是说他们仍然更倾向于对冲基金、私募股权、私募信贷以及其他房地产类投资，让这些东西在组合中占比更大，而不是那些流动性资产？是的，这是个非常……

turns.en: as well. It's impossible for smaller endowments. You really need to get above a significant size to be able to have that full implementation. turns.zh: 这真的很难。对更小的捐赠基金来说是不可能的。你真的需要达到相当大的规模，才能做到那种完整的实施。我们看到的是，尤其在一些较小的捐赠基金中，它们在用我们所说的半流动性载体（semi-liquid vehicles）。也就是说，它们承诺一定的流动性，进入也更容易。

turns.zh: 已经有一整套代表客户投资的另类投资账簿存在，所以你进场时，实际上是在买入一个已经存在的私募资产池。这给了较小的捐赠基金一个稍微容易一点的进场方式，尽管它们也有各自的缺点。

turns.zh: 好的，Anna。就这些东西的发展方式而言，你在 State Street 专注于流动性产品、交易所交易产品。当你看看你们的产品在这里的发展方式时，也许我们不难想象这样一个世界：越来越多的私募或半流动性投资被装进 ETF 外壳。

turns.zh: 我们在很多方面已经见到过：业务发展公司（business development companies，BDC）就是那样；某些私募信贷类 ETF 和共同基金就是那样，那些由 CLO（抵押贷款凭证，collateralized loan obligations）和浮动利率证券支撑的产品。ETF 市场将如何借鉴捐赠基金正在做的事，去演进到下一层级的

Well, Dom, our job as an ETF sponsor and ETF manager is really to make sure that our clients
turns.zh: 产品？还是说我们认为大家都乐于自行发展自己的专业能力，然后由投资顾问来承担那个重活——决定如何配置那些特定资产？嗯，Dom，作为 ETF 发起人和 ETF 管理人，我们的职责其实是确保我们的客户

turns.zh: 明白：我们能替他们做大部分工作，能替他们扛下大部分重活。我举个例子，差不多两年前，我们推出了业内首只——与 Apollo 合作的公开加私募信贷 ETF。那只基金现在把大约 20% 的资产投在私募信贷上。

turns.en: Now, it's all investment grade, it complies with all the liquidity provisions of the 40 years. But it does it in a way that is very thoughtful, meaning we do believe that public market and private markets are converging, are converging right now. And for anyone who believes that this is 10 years ahead, that private markets are going
turns.zh: 这些全是投资级的，符合《1940 年投资公司法》（1940 Act）的所有流动性条款。但它的做法非常深思熟虑，也就是说，我们确实相信公开市场与私募市场正在融合、此刻正在融合。而对于任何认为这还要等 10 年、认为私募市场将会

turns.en: to remain private for a very long time, we kind of disagree with that. I think we are in the middle of that transition, we are in the middle of that convergence right now. turns.zh: 长期保持“私募”状态的人，我们不太同意这种看法。我认为我们正处在这场转变之中，正处在这场融合之中。唯一在阻碍这场融合的，一是缺乏价格发现（price discovery）、价格透明度，二是在某些情况下缺乏流动性。

turns.en: But when you bring an ETF into the mix, when you bring companies like Apollo into the mix, you are creating a market, you are building liquidity. And we brought this product to market, the one thing that changed in the ecosystem is transparency. We disclose the price of each one of these assets every day on our website.
turns.zh: 但当你把 ETF 引入其中、当你把像 Apollo 这样的公司引入其中时，你就在创造一个市场、在建立流动性。而当我们把这款产品推向市场时，生态系统中改变的一件事就是透明度。我们每天在网站上披露这些资产中每一项的价格。

turns.en: So anyone who is working with Apollo, working with others to get access to the same security to the same as the class, to the same piece of private credit now knows exactly how we are pricing it either because we have acquired the assets today from Apollo or because we acquired it in the past and we are pricing it every day.
turns.zh: 所以任何与 Apollo 合作、与其他方合作以获取同一只证券、同一资产类别、同一笔私募信贷的人，现在都确切地知道我们是如何给它定价的——无论是因为我们今天刚从 Apollo 收购了这些资产，还是因为我们过去就收购了它、并且每天都在给它定价。

turns.en: So the combination of these factors is bringing more transparency to the market. With more transparency, liquidity comes. We have seen creations and redemptions coming into this fund with no issues whatsoever when it came to liquidity. To either purchase new assets or relinquishing and selling assets that were already in the market.
turns.zh: 所以这些要素的结合正在给市场带来更多透明度。有了更多透明度，流动性随之而来。我们看到这只基金的申购和赎回，在流动性方面没有遇到任何问题——无论是买入新资产，还是释放并卖出那些已经在市场上的资产。

turns.en: Could I just follow up Anna with that point? turns.zh: Anna，我能就这一点追问一下吗？那是否意味着，即便我看看你们那只私募加公开基金、或者你们那只 UCBG 基金这样规模的 ETF，即便我没看到很大的交易量，作为一名投资者，我是否可以放心地买入或撤出，而不会在市场上造成

turns.en: in the marketplace as the ETF infrastructure evolved enough to where people can feel as though they can go into these products that are supposedly liquid, even if they don't have a lot of trading volume and feel like they're not going to gap it based upon the fact that there's not a lot of trading volume in these particular products.

turns.zh: 嗯，你用了一个在这个行业里极少听到的词，那就是“安全”（safe）。我不认为我们能说任何东西是绝对安全的，或者给出任何保证。我认为，如果你以严谨和勤勉去做这件事，你就能化解其中大部分风险。举个例子，当我们发行时——我们并没有贸然发行这款产品。

turns.zh: 我们花了——我会说——超过两年时间，才有足够的把握把这款产品推向市场。到目前为止，我们经历了申购和赎回，组合中没有出现任何故障。那么，这能否保证将来也不会发生？不能。

turns.en: But right now, the product is behaving as expected. We are actually really pleased with regards to the liquidity of the portfolio, the quality of the assets that we have included in the portfolio. A couple of months ago, the big headlines about a private credit, you know, it's one
turns.zh: 但眼下，这款产品的表现符合预期。对于组合的流动性、以及我们纳入组合的资产质量，我们其实非常满意。几个月前，那些关于私募信贷的大新闻，你知道，这正是那种

turns.en: of those times when you look back at the strategy and you pat yourself in the back saying, we did the right thing. It was not an accident. It was not a coincidence that we decided to really stick with the investment grade segment of the market because we thought when it comes to private credit, quality matters.
turns.zh: 时候：你回过头看这个策略，拍拍自己的背说，我们做对了。这不是偶然。我们决定真正坚守市场的投资级部分，也不是巧合，因为我们认为，就私募信贷而言，质量至关重要。

turns.en: As a matter of fact, the issues that we experienced in the private credit market were not associated with the investment grade segment of the market. So if you do it in a way that is very rigorous, the product should continue to work as expected. We wanted to reinvent fixed income investing.
turns.zh: 事实上，我们在私募信贷市场经历的那些问题，都与市场的投资级部分无关。所以如果你以非常严谨的方式去做，这款产品应该会继续按预期运作。我们想要重新发明固定收益投资。

turns.en: We did not say, oh, we are going to bring a private credit into the market. And then let's cross our fingers that liquidity is going to be there. We had a belief and the belief was, we want to bring high yields. So the higher yields associated with private credit into the fixed income allocation of a client portfolio.
turns.zh: 我们并没有说，哦，我们要把私募信贷带进市场，然后祈祷流动性会在那里。我们有一个信念，那就是：我们想把高收益——也就是私募信贷相关的那些更高收益——带入客户组合的固定收益配置当中。

turns.en: And we want to make sure that investors can benefit from these higher yields. And if you look at the performance of a private, for example, right now, at any given point is delivering about 100 basis points of returns in addition to the benchmark.
turns.zh: 我们想确保投资者能够从这些更高的收益中获益。如果你看看私募的表现，举个例子，眼下在任何一个时点，它都在基准之上额外带来大约 100 个基点（basis points）的回报。

turns.en: So without performing the benchmark by roughly 90 or 100 basis points, which to us is a delivery of the promise we made about reinventing the plus element into core plus. Okay, Mike, I'm going to give you the last word here. Kind of had mentioned the kind of convergence of public and private investing.
turns.zh: 也就是说，跑赢基准大约 90 到 100 个基点，对我们而言，这就是兑现了我们当初的承诺——把“core plus”里的那个“plus”要素重新发明出来。好的，Mike，我要把最后的话语权交给你。（Anna）刚才提到了公开与私募投资的这种融合。

turns.en: of a liquid vehicle, there will be, as we've learned now from private credit, private real estate over the last three or four years, there will be tension between the pricing inside and being able to sell at what's considered NAV. I'm just not sure that that's ever solvable.
turns.zh: 一个流动性载体里，那么——正如我们过去三四年从私募信贷、私募房地产中学到的——在内部定价与能否按所谓的资产净值（NAV）卖出之间，会存在张力。我只是不确定这究竟能不能被解决。

turns.en: We've been telling our clients to put illiquid assets inside of illiquid securities, right? If you're buying something that you expect to be three to five years, put it in a three to five year wrapper. turns.en: There's a lot of interest in the institutional business. I think what we've seen is that over the last five, seven, eight years, ETFs came into the industry as really a retail product. turns.zh: 机构业务这块有很大的兴趣。我想我们看到的是，在过去五、七、八年里，ETF 进入这个行业时，其实是一种散户产品。而那些更大、更成熟的机构就是这么看待它们的，因此他们其实并不太想用 ETF。

turns.en: But we've seen a broad acceptance over the last five years or so with ETFs generally, particularly in traditional securities. In the endowment and foundation space, in what we call other institutional asset space to find benefit and other things like that. So ETFs have come a long way, they're a terrific vehicle. We use them a lot.
turns.zh: 但在过去大约五年里，我们看到 ETF 得到了广泛的接受，尤其是在传统证券方面。在捐赠基金和基金会领域，在我们所说的其他机构资产领域（defined benefit 之类），都能看到它的好处。所以 ETF 已经走了很长的路，它们是很棒的投资载体。我们大量使用它们。

turns.en: We're one of the largest owners of ETFs in our client bases. And so, we spent a lot of diligence trying to understand how ETFs work, what works for specific clients and what doesn't. I still don't think, I disagree with Anna, just a bit here, that the illiquidity features
turns.zh: 在客户群当中，我们是 ETF 最大的持有人之一。所以，我们花了大量尽职调查（diligence）去弄明白 ETF 如何运作、什么对特定客户有效、什么无效。我仍然认为——在这点上我和 Anna 有一点点分歧——那种把非流动性特征

turns.en: inside a liquid vehicle are just going to end up being problematic at some point down the road. All right, Anna, I'm going to give you one final word to respond to that if you want to on that and then we'll call it a day. Yeah, I don't think we are in this agreement. I think that I agree with that.
turns.zh: 放进流动性载体里的做法，终究会在未来某个时点出问题。好的，Anna，我要给你最后一次发言机会，如果你愿意就这一点做个回应，然后我们就到此为止。是的，我不认为我们在这点上有分歧，我想我是同意他的说法的。

turns.en: And this is why you have not seen from us or from others 100% a private credit ETF. And I don't think you are going to see an ETF today that invests 100% of its assets in infrastructure or real estate or inventures because there is a liquidity mismatch.
turns.zh: 这也正是为什么你没有从我们这里、或从别人那里看到 100% 纯私募信贷的 ETF。我也不认为你今天会看到一只把 100% 资产投在基础设施、房地产或风险投资（ventures）里的 ETF，因为存在流动性错配（liquidity mismatch）。

turns.en: But I do think this market circumverging and as soon as one piece of those asset classes will show that level of liquidity that makes us comfortable about striking a delineate, we are going to put it in 20TF and make it really easy for our investors to do one click by and get exposure to that. All right. Okay. The easy button works.
turns.zh: 但我确实认为这个市场正在融合，一旦这些资产类别中的某一块展现出那种让我们放心去划定界限的流动性水平，我们就会把它装进一只 ETF，让我们的投资者只需一键买入就能获得那种敞口，非常容易。好的。行。这个“轻松按钮”确实管用。

turns.en: The easy button does work. Now it's time to round out the conversation with some thoughtful analysis and perspective to help you better understand ETFs with our markets 102 portions of the podcast. An appalia of state street investment management continues with us now.
turns.zh: 这个“轻松按钮”确实管用。现在，是时候用一些有深度的分析和视角来为这场对话收尾了，帮助你更好地理解 ETF——这就是我们播客的 Markets 102 环节。State Street Investment Management 的 Anna Paglia 现在继续留下来和我们一起。

turns.en: One of the things I wanted to key on in that conversation that we had was the convergence of public and private. Now state street, understandably, has already brought a product to market, right? That kind of blends public and private when it comes to the investing alongside private
turns.zh: 在刚才那场对话里，我想重点谈的一件事，就是公开与私募的融合。而 State Street，可以理解，已经把一款产品推向了市场，对吧？它在投资上把公开和私募融合了起来，还与私募

turns.en: equity, giant Apollo and with some of the more liquid investments that you have in the public markets. PRIV is the ticker there. Is it safe to say, and I use safe sparingly because in investing, safe is never a word that you want to use heavily, but is it safe to say that the ETF market is evolving
turns.zh: 股权巨头 Apollo 联手，并结合了你在公开市场上拥有的一些流动性更好的投资。那里的代码是 PRIV。能不能这么说——我用“安全”这个词很谨慎，因为在投资里，“安全”从来不是一个你想重用的词——但能不能说，ETF 市场正在演进

turns.en: to a point where it is trying to become a lot more encompassing of the types of investment strategies and customers that it could possibly serve? Well, Dom, I would say that this is not really a new story. We have seen in the past how the convergence between liquid and liquid was either accelerated or created by ETFs coming to market.
turns.zh: 到这样一个地步：它正试图变得更加包罗万象，去覆盖它可能服务的各种投资策略和各类客户？嗯，Dom，我会说这其实并不是什么新故事。我们过去就见过，流动性与非流动性之间的融合，是如何被 ETF 的上市所加速、甚至所创造的。

turns.en: I think it's kind of misguided to think about the market as something that is a liquid will continue to be a liquid forever and something that is a liquid will only be the instrument for daily and other products. If you go back 10 or 15 years, at that time ETFs were only rule-based, large cap equity securities index only.
turns.zh: 我认为，把市场想成“非流动性的东西会永远非流动、流动性的东西只会是每日申赎那类产品的工具”，这种想法有点被误导了。如果你回到 10 年或 15 年前，那时候 ETF 还只是基于规则的、仅限大盘股证券的指数产品。

turns.en: The market has evolved and the ETF market has actually created a liquidity in segments where liquidity was not and I will give you a couple of examples, fixed income. 15 years ago, nobody believed that you could buy bonds and put them into an ETF because the bond market was not liquid, was not liquid at all.
turns.zh: 市场已经演进，而 ETF 市场实际上在一些原本没有流动性的板块里创造出了流动性。我给你举几个例子：固定收益。15 年前，没人相信你能买入债券并把它们装进一只 ETF，因为债券市场没有流动性，完全没有。

turns.en: But right now, thanks to the ETFs pushing liquidity and creating an ecosystem for some of those bonds, bonds that were illiquid 15 years ago are liquid, emerging markets. But I thought 15 years ago that retail investors could get access to emerging markets equity securities, live aside emerging markets debts.
turns.zh: 但眼下，多亏了 ETF 推动流动性、并为其中一些债券建立起一个生态系统，那些 15 年前非流动性的债券现在有了流动性。再看新兴市场（emerging markets）。15 年前，谁会想到散户投资者能够接触到新兴市场股票证券，更别提新兴市场债务了。

turns.en: But then the ETF came along and the creation and the existence of the ETF was such that an entire ecosystem was built around that. So now something that was inherently illiquid became liquid enough to be placed into an ETF. And I do think that the history tends to repeat itself because what we are seeing today
turns.zh: 但后来 ETF 出现了，ETF 的创设和存在，使得一整个生态系统围绕它建立了起来。所以现在，一种本质上非流动性的东西，变得足够流动，可以被装进一只 ETF。我确实认为历史往往会重演，因为我们今天所看到的，

turns.en: is just a repeat of that process where private credit is becoming a more transparent and more liquid because ETFs are pushing the envelope and it's not just the wrapper, it's not just the content, it's the entire partnership scenario and the ecosystem around that.
turns.zh: 只不过是那个过程的又一次重演：私募信贷正变得更透明、更有流动性，因为 ETF 在不断突破边界（pushing the envelope）。而且这不仅仅是那个外壳，不仅仅是内容本身，而是整个合作格局，以及围绕它建立起来的生态系统。

turns.en: We are working with private markets and private credit issuers, originators. We are asking them to make those assets more transparent and more liquid. We have seen big companies like Apollo with the help of the infrastructure. For example, in this case, I was a state street bank starting to publish daily nav for their private funds.
turns.zh: 我们正在与私募市场和私募信贷的发行人、发起机构（originators）合作。我们正在要求他们让这些资产更透明、更有流动性。我们已经看到像 Apollo 这样的大公司，在基础设施的帮助下——比如在这个案例里，是 State Street 银行——开始为它们的私募基金每日公布资产净值（NAV）。

turns.en: So this is all new and this is all really improving the liquidity of that as a class. Now it doesn't happen by magic. You are not going to see private credit, infrastructure, real estate, become liquid from one day to the next. This is just a process by which you take something a liquid, you create the ecosystem around
turns.zh: 所以这一切都是全新的，也确实是在改善这一资产类别的流动性。但这不会靠魔法发生。你不会看到私募信贷、基础设施、房地产一夜之间变得有流动性。这只是一个过程：你把一种非流动性的东西，围绕它建立起生态系统，

turns.en: that, you create the infrastructure and it becomes liquid enough to be placed into an ETF. I started my Wall Street career in the late 90s and I remember the days of as an investment advisor having to ping around bond inventory sheets to try to figure out who had what
turns.zh: 建立起基础设施，然后它变得足够流动，可以被装进一只 ETF。我在 90 年代末开始了我的华尔街生涯，我记得那时作为一名投资顾问，得到处去问债券的库存清单，想弄清楚谁手里有什么货、

turns.en: went and where and then trying to make those investments, buying and selling, who had an axe to grind, who wanted to buy these types of bonds. But you fast forward 20 some years later, the technological innovation of markets, the speed at which transactions happen, the kind of infrastructure around it.
turns.zh: 去了哪里，然后再去做那些投资、买进卖出，谁有减持的需求（an axe to grind）、谁想买这类债券。但你快进二十多年之后，市场的技术创新、交易发生的速度、围绕它的那种基础设施，

turns.en: It's all part of that ecosystem that you just mentioned right now. If you had mentioned bonds before and that's the reason why I'm bringing it up, you had mentioned bonds before as being one of those formerly fairly illiquid mechanisms or asset classes that became more and more liquid because of the evolution of ETFs.
turns.zh: 全都是你刚才提到的那个生态系统的一部分。你之前提到过债券——这也正是我提起它的原因——你之前把债券列为那种从前相当缺乏流动性、却因为 ETF 的演进而变得越来越有流动性的机制或资产类别之一。

turns.en: If you build it, they will come. If you build bond portfolios and exchange trade them and other people do the same, the creation redemption process creates that ecosystem effect where there's more liquidity. If you use that as an example and you use your best judgment as the chief business officer
turns.zh: “只要你建好，他们自会来。”如果你搭建债券组合并让它们交易所交易，别人也这么做，那么申购赎回（creation/redemption）流程就会创造出那种生态系统效应，带来更多流动性。如果你以此为例，运用你作为首席业务官

turns.en: at State Street Investment Management, when do you think we could see more liquidity akin to what's in fixed income markets now brought to certain private credit, private equity type investments? Wow. That's a big question. I don't have a crystal ball. But I will tell you, to me, we are looking at five years, five years-ish, type of time
turns.zh: （在 State Street Investment Management）的最佳判断，你认为我们什么时候能看到更多流动性——类似于现在固定收益市场里的那种——被带到某些私募信贷、私募股权类投资上？哇，这是个大问题。我没有水晶球。但我会告诉你，在我看来，我们面对的是一个五年、五年左右的时间

turns.en: window. And I tell you that because the market is already moving that way. Because in the last two years, I have never heard more questions than those that I have received in the last two years about using private assets into ETFs. And these questions are not just coming from investors in the different channels.
turns.zh: 窗口。我这么说，是因为市场已经在朝那个方向移动了。因为在过去两年里，我从没收到过比这两年更多的、关于把私募资产装进 ETF 的问题。而且这些问题不仅仅来自不同渠道的投资者，

turns.en: They are not just coming from private assets firms. They are coming from many different places within the ecosystem. So I do think that a number of smart people are already looking at and how to solve for the liquidity problem. I also think that I want to go back to something that you said because I'm a lawyer by trade.
turns.zh: 也不仅仅来自私募资产公司，而是来自生态系统中许多不同的地方。所以我确实认为，已经有一批聪明人在研究如何解决流动性问题了。我还想回到你说过的一句话，因为我本行是律师。

turns.en: So I tend to be very conservative when it comes to liquidity and investor protection. I don't think that this is a matter of building it and they will come. I don't think that they come only because you build it. I think this is a process of building it only once you know that they will come. And how do you know that?
turns.zh: 所以在流动性和投资者保护方面，我往往非常保守。我不认为这是一个“只要你建好，他们自会来”的问题。我不认为他们仅仅因为你建好了就会来。我认为这是一个过程：只有当你知道他们会来时，你才去建。那你怎么知道他们会来呢？

turns.en: You have already worked with the ecosystem. I don't think we would have launched PRIV. We would not have launched the PRIV without Apollo, without having confidence in the ecosystem and the liquidity of the assets that we are buying, investment grade assets originated by Apollo.
turns.zh: 你得已经和这个生态系统合作过了。我不认为我们会推出 PRIV。如果没有 Apollo，如果对我们所买资产——由 Apollo 发起的投资级资产——的生态系统和流动性没有信心，我们是不会推出 PRIV 的。

turns.en: I don't think that we would have launched senior loans products without a blackstone. So you build it only when you have confidence in the liquidity of the ecosystem. Now it doesn't matter that the ecosystem cannot get better. I'll give you an example since we talked about PRIV.
turns.zh: 我也不认为，如果没有 Blackstone，我们会推出优先级贷款（senior loans）产品。所以，只有当你对生态系统的流动性有信心时，你才去建。这并不意味着生态系统不能变得更好。既然谈到了 PRIV，我给你举个例子。

turns.en: PRIV can invest up to 30% of the portfolio in private credit. We are now at 20%. We are not using the entire 30% allocation. And the reason for that is we want to make sure that whatever we buy is high quality and it's liquid that meets all of our internal requirements. So to me it's a combination of different things.
turns.zh: PRIV 最多可以把组合的 30% 投在私募信贷上。我们现在是 20%。我们没有用满整个 30% 的额度。原因在于，我们想确保我们买的一切都是高质量、有流动性、并满足我们所有内部要求的。所以对我来说，这是多种因素的结合。

turns.en: Do you have a community of broker dealers? Who can come together in a marketplace, so to speak, and accelerate the paperwork, the diligence, the review process, so that these assets can be transferred on T plus 1 or T plus 3 basis. Do you have enough transparency so that the broker dealer community will feel comfortable
turns.zh: 你有没有一个经纪交易商（broker dealers）群体，能够在一个市场上——可以这么说——聚集起来，加快文书工作、尽职调查、审核流程，从而让这些资产能以 T+1 或 T+3 的基础完成转让？你有没有足够的透明度，让经纪交易商群体感到放心，

turns.en: buying the assets from the fund and not from other asset managers or private market providers? So if you are confident about the movement in the ecosystem, then you also feel confident that that product at that moment in time can meet the liquidity promises that it made to investors.
turns.zh: 愿意从这只基金、而不是从其他资产管理人或私募市场提供方那里买入这些资产？所以，如果你对生态系统中的这种动向有信心，那你也会相信，那款产品在那个时点上能够兑现它对投资者做出的流动性承诺。

turns.en: And maybe the next iteration is not going to be up to 30% of private credit. Maybe can go up to 60%. Maybe in five years we are going to have a 100% private credit ETF. And this is part of a transition and a process where we are going to work really, really hard with all of the ecosystem, all the participants.
turns.zh: 也许下一个迭代版本不会是私募信贷上限 30%，也许可以到 60%。也许五年后我们会有一只 100% 私募信贷的 ETF。而这是转变和过程的一部分，在这个过程中，我们会非常非常努力地与整个生态系统、所有参与者协作。

turns.en: And when we get there, hopefully we are going to be the first ones to crack that code, not because we are the smartest guys in the room. We are never going to be the smartest guys in the room, but we are clearly going to be the ones that are going to work the hardest to get there.
turns.zh: 而当我们到达那一步时，希望我们会是第一个破解那道难题的人——不是因为我们是在场最聪明的人。我们永远不会是在场最聪明的人，但我们显然会是那个为了抵达目标而努力最狠的人。

turns.en: So it leads me to my next question, because if you look at the way that you described the current state and the anticipated future state of the ETF market, you have brought a couple of products to market that have garnered some headlines because they are fairly at the tip of the spear.
turns.zh: 这就引出了我的下一个问题。因为如果你看看你描述 ETF 市场当前状态和预期未来状态的方式，你们已经把几款产品推向了市场，它们赢得了一些头条关注，因为它们相当处于前沿（at the tip of the spear）。

turns.en: We had mentioned during the online show for ETF Edge, the University of California, Blue Gold, Endowment Process ETF, the 90s stock 10 bond allocation UCBG ticker. You mentioned PRIV, another type of product that is relatively new to its kind of market place effect. From your standpoint, you look at business development in ETFs.
turns.zh: 我们在 ETF Edge 的线上节目里提到过 University of California Blue and Gold 捐赠基金 ETF，那个 90% 股票、10% 债券配置、代码为 UCBG 的产品。你也提到了 PRIV，另一种相对新颖、带有某种市场效应的产品。从你的角度看，你看看 ETF 领域的业务发展，

turns.en: You have kind of seen what has happened over the past 10 years, the advent of actively managed, the prevalence of it now, now kind of buffer related to find outcome based ETFs, that sort of thing. What do you think is kind of like that next story or that next frontier when it comes
turns.zh: 你大致看到了过去 10 年发生了什么：主动管理型（actively managed）ETF 的出现、如今的普及，还有那种与 buffer 相关的、基于目标结果（defined outcome）的 ETF 之类的东西。你认为，当谈到 ETF 时，下一个故事、下一个前沿

turns.en: to ETFs and what types of strategies do you see developing in the say next 3 to 5 years for ETFs? Tom, I have been in this industry for 28 years now and I am an ETF nerd and the reason why I love this industry is because this industry is never static. It never stops, it's never one thing and one thing only.
turns.zh: 会是什么？未来三到五年里，你会看到 ETF 发展出哪些类型的策略？Dom，我在这个行业已经 28 年了，我是个 ETF 迷（nerd）。我之所以热爱这个行业，是因为它从不静止。它从不停歇，从不只是单一的一件事。

turns.en: It evolves and it does not evolve from the manufacturer's standpoint. Back in the day, the asset managers decided, I have a new strategy, I have a high conviction on this strategy, I'm going to sell the strategy to my clients. Right now, the product development process is the opposite, where the idea comes from clients.
turns.zh: 它在演进，而且这种演进并不是从制造商的角度出发的。在过去，资产管理人会说：我有一个新策略，我对这个策略很有信心，我要把它卖给我的客户。而现在，产品开发流程正好相反——想法来自客户。

turns.en: It's not just big institutional clients saying, I want to create a strategy that looks like X. It comes from many different channels, including retail channels, retail investors used to be 5% to 7% of our flows, right now are between 20% and 25% of our flows. And buffer the ETFs, downside protection products or derivative income products.
turns.zh: 这不仅仅是大型机构客户说“我想创造一个长得像 X 的策略”，它来自许多不同的渠道，包括散户渠道。散户投资者过去占我们资金流量的 5% 到 7%，现在则占我们资金流量的 20% 到 25%。而那些 buffer ETF、下行保护型产品或衍生品收益型产品，

turns.en: That was not an idea that came from asset managers. This is an idea that came from investors. There was anxiety, especially during the pandemic, about market volatility. There was a need, there was a concern coming from our investors about caping their liability,
turns.zh: 并不是资产管理人想出来的点子，而是来自投资者的点子。尤其是在疫情期间，人们对市场波动感到焦虑。有一种需求、有一种来自我们投资者的关切，就是想要给自己的损失设上限（capping their liability）、

turns.en: caping the downside, and they were willing to pay up a little bit on the upside just to have that piece of mind. There was a need coming from our clients about income, people need a paycheck. And that really pushed the creative juices of ETF providers to say, we can do that with an ETF.
turns.zh: 给下行风险封顶，为此他们愿意在上行收益上稍微让出一点，只求一份安心。我们的客户还有一种关于收益（income）的需求——人们需要一份“工资”。这真的激发了 ETF 提供方的创造力，让他们说：这个我们能用 ETF 来做。

turns.en: Seven years ago, eight years ago, if you wanted to go to a family office or an advisor and talk about derivatives into an ETF, that was going to be a really, really hard conversation to have. Because at that time, the world ETF, the three-leaders ETFs, we associated with low cost,
turns.zh: 七年前、八年前，如果你想去找一个家族办公室（family office）或顾问，跟他们谈把衍生品放进 ETF，那会是一场非常非常艰难的对话。因为在那个时候，ETF 这个词、这三个字母，我们把它和低成本、

turns.en: easy to understand, rule-based, straight-egg with your straight-fix income. Having a derivative overlay over those products, it was going to be a really hard conversation to have. Today, it's not that hard anymore. So the industry is evolving at pace with client needs.
turns.zh: 容易理解、基于规则、直白的股票、直白的固定收益联系在一起。要在这些产品之上叠加一层衍生品（derivative overlay），那会是一场很艰难的对话。而今天，它已经没那么难了。所以这个行业正在与客户需求同步演进。

turns.en: So if I think about the next five years or ten years, clearly, we spoke about public and private. So I'm not going to go back to that. But the other thing that we are working on is retirement. We just launched a mutual fund share class of our SPIM, our S&P 500 fund. Wait, you launched a mutual fund on an ETF platform? Within. Right.
turns.zh: 所以如果我想未来五年或十年，显然我们谈过了公开与私募，我就不再回到那个话题。但我们正在做的另一件事是退休（retirement）。我们刚刚为我们的 SPYM、也就是我们的 S&P 500 基金，推出了一个共同基金份额类别（mutual fund share class）。等等，你在一个 ETF 平台上推出了共同基金？在其之内。对。

turns.en: But why? I mean, you're going to tell me. I'm sure. But why would you go backwards? Some people will say backwards. I'm a former mutual fund guy, so I never think of it as moving backwards. But it doesn't seem as though people talk about mutual funds that much these days when they have ETFs available.
turns.zh: 但为什么呢？我是说，你肯定会告诉我的。但为什么要往回走？有些人会说这是往回走。我是个曾经做共同基金的人，所以我从不觉得这是倒退。但现在人们既然有了 ETF，似乎就不怎么谈论共同基金了。

turns.en: So why go with the mutual fund of an S&P 500 product? That's a really good question, Dom. And I do think that the industry is asking the wrong question. It's not about a legal wrapper. This is something that we have been debating for 30 years. Mewsha funds versus ETFs, active versus passive. It's not one thing versus the other.
turns.zh: 那为什么要给一个 S&P 500 产品做共同基金呢？这是个非常好的问题，Dom。我确实认为，行业问错了问题。这不是关于法律外壳的问题。这是我们争论了 30 年的东西：共同基金对 ETF、主动对被动。这并不是非此即彼的事。

turns.en: Let's go back to principles. What problem are we solving for? We are solving a problem of fragmentation. Because at State Street, we can launch strategies in many different wrappers. We have index mutual funds, we have CITs, we have ETFs, we have active strategies. So we are not constrained by the legal wrapper.
turns.zh: 让我们回到原则。我们要解决的是什么问题？我们要解决的是碎片化（fragmentation）的问题。因为在 State Street，我们可以用许多不同的外壳来推出策略。我们有指数共同基金、有 CIT（集合投资信托，collective investment trusts）、有 ETF、有主动策略。所以我们并不受法律外壳的约束。

turns.en: But two and a half years ago, we asked ourselves, is this effective? Because whenever you have a fragmentation, you have to add cost. I mean, fragmentation is not free of charge. The fragmentation is expensive. Now, again, look at the market. DC plants, we are looking at segment at the segment of the market with a 30% exposure
turns.zh: 但两年半前，我们问自己：这样有效吗？因为每当你有碎片化，你就得增加成本。我是说，碎片化不是免费的，碎片化是昂贵的。那么，再看看市场。DC 计划（defined contribution plans）——我们看的是市场里那一个板块，它对大盘股有 30% 的敞口，
